headline: Austin robotaxi fleet: 50 active rider vehicles + 38 Cybercabs in test fleet; unsupervised ride rate hits 66.7% — 28 of 42 rides in last 7 days with no safety driver; up from 59.0% on May 8 and 27.8% on May 6; fleet now operating unsupervised during evening hours for first time as of May 4; pace of autonomous operational maturity accelerating sharply across both daytime and night sessions (robotaxitracker.com / Teslarati)

Analyst projects 95M Tesla FSD subscribers and $1 trillion annual revenue by 2038 — near-term gating milestone: 10.6M subscribers by 2030 (vs ~1.28M active today); model assumes dramatic FSD adoption acceleration as robotaxi network scales and unsupervised driving matures; gap between today and 2030 target requires ~8x subscriber growth in 4 years; bull-case valuation framework reinforces Tesla as AI platform rather than automaker (basenor.com)

Tesla builds last-ever Model S and Model X at Fremont — factory line now converting to Optimus production; Fremont line targeting 1M robots/year at full capacity; Signature Edition final delivery event for existing reservation holders originally set May 12 but has since been postponed; end of Tesla's flagship luxury EV era marks the beginning of its robotics-first manufacturing era (evxl.co / notateslaapp / Electrek / TeslaNorth)

TSLA closes at $428.35 on May 8 (+4.02%) — 4-week high; strongest single-session gain since April; driven by resilient April jobs report lifting all risk assets (SPY +0.83%, QQQ +2.34%), China April deliveries +36% YoY, and ongoing Intel 14A/Terafab chip partnership narrative; stock recovered ~15% from post-earnings $373 low in under 3 weeks (primaryignition.com / Yahoo Finance)

EU FSD bloc-wide approval confirmed July at earliest, October more realistic — TCMV has no vote scheduled; Tesla needs representatives of 15/27 EU member states AND 65% of bloc population to vote yes; Nordic regulators raised concerns over FSD allowing speeding and hands-free driving on icy roads at Brussels session; Ars Technica: 'Chinese and European regulators require premarket approval' and European FSD product differs meaningfully from US version; Tesla's Q2/Q3 internal approval target under material uncertainty (Reuters / Ars Technica)

Tesla begins internal testing of FSD v14.3.2 in China — first concrete testing milestone after repeated regulatory delays; Q3 2026 approval now cited as official target after missing Q1 and Q2 windows; Tesla building Baidu HD map integration per Beijing requirement that foreign firms not conduct independent HD mapping in China; only partial public-road test authorization held; China represents Tesla's largest untapped FSD subscriber market (eletric-vehicles.com / letsdatascience)

SpaceX formally files plan revealing Terafab chip factory costs $55B–$119B — joint Tesla/SpaceX semiconductor facility in Texas enters formal planning phase; research fab at Giga Texas (~$3B) will produce AI5-class chips in small batches; full Terafab scope $55B minimum with total exceeding $119B; Intel 14A process confirmed; SpaceX filing notes 'no assurance' on timeline execution; one of the largest private infrastructure investments in history if fully built (CNBC / Bloomberg / Reuters)

WattEV orders 370 Tesla Semi trucks in a landmark $100M deal — California's largest-ever single electric truck order; 50 trucks deliver in 2026 with full fleet by end 2027; 300+ units to support Port of Oakland freight electrification; WattEV CEO cited Tesla Semi's 'cost, performance, and availability' as decisive factors vs. competitors; signals major fleet-scale enterprise adoption accelerating alongside Gigafactory Nevada volume ramp (Teslarati / ACT Expo)
